clauses.normalized_text: IP version 6 (IPv6) is a new version of the Internet Protocol (IP), designed as the successor to IP version 4 (IPv4) [RFC791].

clauses.normalized_text: The changes from IPv4 to IPv6 fall primarily into the following categories:

clauses.normalized_text: o Expanded Addressing Capabilities
clauses.raw_text: o Expanded Addressing Capabilities

clauses.normalized_text: IPv6 increases the IP address size from 32 bits to 128 bits, to support more levels of addressing hierarchy, a much greater number of addressable nodes, and simpler autoconfiguration of addresses.
clauses.raw_text: IPv6 increases the IP address size from 32 bits to 128 bits, to support more levels of addressing hierarchy, a much greater number of addressable nodes, and simpler autoconfiguration of addresses.

clauses.normalized_text: The scalability of multicast routing is improved by adding a "scope" field to multicast addresses.
clauses.raw_text: The scalability of multicast routing is improved by adding a "scope" field to multicast addresses.

clauses.normalized_text: And a new type of address called an "anycast address" is defined; it is used to send a packet to any one of a group of nodes.
clauses.raw_text: And a new type of address called an "anycast address" is defined; it is used to send a packet to any one of a group of nodes.

clauses.normalized_text: o Header Format Simplification
clauses.raw_text: o Header Format Simplification

clauses.normalized_text: Some IPv4 header fields have been dropped or made optional, to reduce the common-case processing cost of packet handling and to limit the bandwidth cost of the IPv6 header.
clauses.raw_text: Some IPv4 header fields have been dropped or made optional, to reduce the common-case processing cost of packet handling and to limit the bandwidth cost of the IPv6 header.

clauses.normalized_text: o Improved Support for Extensions and Options
clauses.raw_text: o Improved Support for Extensions and Options

clauses.normalized_text: Changes in the way IP header options are encoded allows for more efficient forwarding, less stringent limits on the length of options, and greater flexibility for introducing new options in the future.
clauses.raw_text: Changes in the way IP header options are encoded allows for more efficient forwarding, less stringent limits on the length of options, and greater flexibility for introducing new options in the future.

clauses.normalized_text: o Flow Labeling Capability
clauses.raw_text: o Flow Labeling Capability

clauses.normalized_text: A new capability is added to enable the labeling of sequences of packets that the sender requests to be treated in the network as a single flow.

clauses.normalized_text: o Authentication and Privacy Capabilities
clauses.raw_text: o Authentication and Privacy Capabilities

clauses.normalized_text: IPv6 requires that every link in the Internet have an MTU of 1280 octets or greater.
